title: Impact of Normalisation of Global Supply Chains on Singapore's Seaport
what_it_is: Impact of Normalisation of Global Supply Chains on Singapore's Seaport

sections.label: Port capacity and container throughput
sections.summary: MPA, PSA and unions added berths, workers and equipment; Singapore handled a record 37.5 million TEUs in 2021 and operates at about 85% of 44 million TEU capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: MPA worked closely with PSA and the unions to open additional berths and yards, and deployed more port workers and equipment to handle surges in container volumes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Our port handled a record high container throughput of 37.5 million 20-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Our container port is currently operating at about 85% of its maximum handling capacity of 44 million TEUs per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: There is enough buffer to meet short-term increases in demand from shipping lines.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: As more berths at Tuas Port are completed, our handling capacity will increase further and provide sufficient capacity to handle future growth in volumes.

sections.label: Tuas Port technology and manpower
sections.summary: At Tuas Port, technology including autonomous vehicles and productivity improvements lets one crane operator run multiple quay cranes and reduces manpower needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: At Tuas Port, for example, we are not only going to make it a more sustainable and more efficient port, we are also deploying technology that will reduce the need for manpower, for example, drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We use autonomous vehicles to help us to transport the cargo within the port.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We use productivity improvements so that one crane operator is able to operate multiple quay cranes at the same time.

sections.label: Shipping network effect
sections.summary: More ships calling and more shipping lines hubbing at Singapore create a network effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Because the more ships call at Singapore, the more shipping lines hub at Singapore, there is a network effect.
